labels.label: rem:hypothesis_model_spaces_necessary
labels.notes: DEC-87(b) reads 'Hypothesis (C) for the model spaces' as theo:local_virt_tame's 'Aut(X~_alpha) acts T_alpha-continuously' (l.1975). GX.hypothesis_model_spaces_necessary proves the remark's counterexample under that reading, for every alpha with 0 < alpha and alpha != 2*pi, which is the paper's theta in R_+ minus {0, 2pi}. The instance is the remark's own: the spinless massive particle MassCyl alpha with G = Isom_0. The structure hypothesis is satisfiable: GX.exists_isMassiveStructure. What the theorem proves: sing = the axis; the model is tame; Phi : M~ ~= D_inf x R over E_alpha; three topologies are tamifying (IsTamifyingTopology carries <= natural, first countable, LPC and (A)-(D); all seven fields are built in massCyl_isTamifying_tamTop): the natural topology, the transported BTZ topology btzGenTop (= natural inf generateFrom {r theta^2 < lambda}, l.1953), and T' = mixedTop(T, {t>0}), which is literally 'generated by the natural one and T|{t>0}' (pullTamTop_eq_mixedTop). Field (C) is the remark's 'Galois group preserves T''. Finally there is f in aeAutMapsMax (time shift by 2) that is T-continuous and not T'-continuous. So Aut-continuity is not implied by tamifying, which is the reading's content. The remark's own unproved claim that T' is again tamifying is now built. The l.2146 sentence (the proof fails because T_{U,V,phi} depends on V) is a meta-claim about a proof. SCOPE (c) discloses this and points to the abstract mechanism GX.hypothesis_model_spaces_mechanism. I accept that this carries no further assertion. Mark justified.

labels.label: rem:quotient_virtually_tame
labels.notes: DEC-87(c) extends DEC-71's 'N Galoisian' to l.2154 and reads 'isomorphic' as homeomorphic. Both readings are exactly the ones the decl uses. GX.quotient_virtually_tame_galoisian' takes the following. T is any tamifying topology on M~, which is at least as strong as 'M virtually tame'. N is any Galoisian branched covering possibly branched over sing M; N being T2/LPC/first countable is §3's standing assumption (l.811) and DEC-66(a). Pj : M~ -> N is obtained from prop:universality (GX.maxBranched_universal); the unprimed GX.quotient_virtually_tame_galoisian proves the conclusion for EVERY continuous surjection over M, which is stronger. D is any injective map continuous for coinduced Pj T, with a holonomy rho (IsHolonomyOf). Pj_*T is finer than the natural topology of N, so this is weaker than continuity of a developing map, and no (G,X)-morphism property is required. The conclusion: Quotient(orbit setoid of rho on range D) ~=_t M, sending [D n] to pi_N n, where D(N) carries devImageTop = (induced from X) inf generateFrom {D-images of Pj_*T-open sets}. That is the third item verbatim. The second item ('N endowed with the quotient of T') is coinduced Pj T, and the first ('acts via the holonomy of D') is the orbit setoid of rho. No extra hypothesis is left outside the ruling, and every hypothesis is satisfiable (N = M~, the universal case). Mark justified.

labels.label: rem:intuitively_spread_thinner_than
labels.notes: DEC-87(d) reads the remark 'in the setting of lem:spread_top'. WP-40d's ruling question named GX.intuitively_spread_thinner_of_local and its restriction, and the author answered 'Accept (a)-(e)', so the ruling covers this exact form. The decl takes exactly the hypotheses of GX.spread_top_of_local (DEC-80(c)). Its conclusion is IsGreatest {sigma' | sigma' <= T_{M~^S} and IsSpread sigma' T p} (strongPullTop p T). In mathlib's order a coarser topology is larger, so this says p^*T is the coarsest spread topology among those finer than the natural one. The restriction to sigma' <= T_M is the paper's 'strong topology' convention (l.1981: the strong topology is the thinner of the two). It is genuinely needed even inside the lemma's setting. I checked this independently: for a non-injective covering p with T = T_N, sigma' = p^{-1}T_N satisfies GX.IsSpread (continuous, and generated by its components of preimages) and is strictly coarser than T_M = p^*T. So the restriction is not an avoidable weakening. The 'However' sentence is GX.cex_component_not_strongPull_connected: p = id on R, T = R cut at 0 (T <= usual is proved). R, the usual component of p^{-1}(R), is not p^*T-preconnected. This witnesses 'the definition does not guarantee'. 'Point (e) is thus non-trivial' is commentary. The two counterexamples to the unrestricted reading are kept and their status is disclosed (SCOPE (f)). Mark justified.
